28fc5cf85d.q: What is Amazon's water positive goal for data center operations and how far along is the company toward achieving it?
28fc5cf85d.a: Amazon announced a water positive goal for AWS data center operations, meaning they want to put more water back into communities than they take out. As of the end of 2024, Amazon is 75% towards meeting this water positive goal for their data center operations. The goal is structured around three pillars: reduce water consumption, reuse recycled water instead of potable water, and replenish water resources through community projects.

e207302f8b.q: Why do Amazon data centers use water and what is the efficiency comparison to industry averages?
e207302f8b.a: Amazon uses water strategically on the hottest days—less than 10% of the year—to power evaporative cooling systems that reduce peak energy use by 25 to 35 percent, which helps meet climate goals and maintains grid health. On the other 90% of the year, data centers use outside air for cooling without any water. Amazon's water efficiency metric is measured at seven times more efficient than the industry average, withdrawing less than 5 million gallons per year per data center—equivalent to about a couple of restaurants.
